patterns.key_values: 5-item flat nav source list (Rules/Templates/Activity/Settings/About), SF Symbol + label, ~40pt rows, selection = solid brand-hue rounded fill w/ white text+glyph; no section headers in sidebar

grouped rule list: tracked-UPPERCASE section headers + inset rounded card groups; row = [status-toggle | brand icon | bold title / tertiary middle-dot metadata subtitle]; ~50-56pt 2-line rows; disabled rows dim in place

signature_moves: Single-hue brand commitment: one orange-red (~#E5401C) carries the entire identity — solid saturated sidebar-selection fill (not translucent), the file-with-gear rule icons, replacing the system accent everywhere. The app's whole personality in one color.

Status-toggle-as-traffic-light: a custom green(on)/red(off) pill per rule row doubles as an at-a-glance enabled/disabled indicator — the one place saturated color is spent in the content field, and it's spent on meaning.

Rule-as-sentence subtitle: each row's metadata reads as plain English (condition . action . destination — 'Extension is .dmg . Move to Trash . Downloads'), so an automation config is scannable without decoding a form.
defects: Tracked-uppercase section headers — non-native tell (HIG wants sentence-case system-font secondary headers) and a mild scanning cost (ALL-CAPS uniform word shapes slow reading).

Non-system accent binding — brand orange-red overrides the user's controlAccentColor for selection/focus; internally consistent house style, but breaks the 'accent is the user's' native rule (record as tell + correction, borderline defect vs. brand signature).

Color-meaning collision (minor) — RED used for a merely-disabled rule toggle; red conventionally signals destructive/error, so an inert disabled rule can misread as a problem. Gray-off would be the safer native reading.
Contrast Dilution (soft, #9/#10) — tertiary subtitle ~4:1 and hairline separators <3:1 against the dark ground (estimated); disabled row is intentionally low.
iOS-grouped-table density on Mac (native#5) — tall 2-line inset-card rows import an iPhone-Settings rhythm rather than compact desktop list density.

aesthetic.direction: Neo-grotesque product utility in dark neutral, but rotated OFF the reflexive electric/acid accent onto a warm orange-red brand hue — a disciplined charcoal field where one saturated warm color does all the identity work; committed (not template-default) via the single-hue commitment and the custom status-toggle language.

psychology: Von Restorff + signal-detection — against a disciplined neutral charcoal field, the single saturated selection and the green/red status dots are the only loud things, so the eye lands exactly on state and current location; color spent only where it means something.

Tesler's Law / recognition-over-recall — the plain-English metadata subtitle spells out each rule's full logic (condition/action/destination) so the user never reconstructs an opaque config from memory; irreducible complexity absorbed into the label.

Jakob's Law (partial violation) — the inset-grouped list + tracked-uppercase headers + pill toggles import iPhone-Settings conventions onto the Mac; familiar to iOS users, but it deviates from Mac-native list expectations rather than meeting them.
Hick's Law — a 5-item sidebar keeps the primary navigation decision tiny; richness lives inside the Rules list (a browse/scan surface), correctly leaving option density there.
Aesthetic-usability — the coherent dark palette and tidy row rhythm buy perceived usability for a 'set a rule once and forget it' tool where trust-at-a-glance matters.
notes: SINGLE surface, SINGLE mode (dark) — the app WINDOW embedded in the right ~50% of a 1200x630 marketing OG cover; no separate shot-* files were supplied (gallery empty). The window is perspective-warped a few degrees and bleeds off the right/bottom, so ALL pixel values are (estimated) with wide error bars — no clean measured tokens beyond the 1200x630 cover aspect. LINEAGE IS GENUINELY AMBIGUOUS: strong iOS idioms (inset-grouped cards, tracked-uppercase headers, pill toggles, tall 2-line rows) point at Catalyst OR an iOS-first SwiftUI-multiplatform app shipped to Mac; the SF Symbol sidebar-toggle + big brand-filled SwiftUI-style List selection + genuine traffic lights lean SwiftUI-native. Recorded as native/low-confidence with Catalyst NOT excluded — its iOS-derived list grammar must be treated as tells+corrections, NOT learned as mac canon regardless of the final lineage call. ERA 'big-sur' = the modern flat-rounded-dark idiom; NO confirmable Liquid Glass (flat opaque chrome — legitimate for a utility, absence is not a defect), and dark-mode humility means glass-vs-solid is unresolvable from this still anyway. The app icon (orange-red folded file tossed onto a dark curved shelf/smile) was digested separately as autoshelf-icon.json — referenced here only as brand-color corroboration (#E5401C family), not re-digested. Marketing copy ('watches your folders and moves files') is context, not evidence. No promotions possible from one app/one surface.
